web_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What does Manorama Industries actually do, is it a genuine compounder or a cocoa-cycle trade, and what exact action should new and existing capital take at ₹1,984.10?

epigraph.quote: Great compounding stories are rarely hidden in obscure spreadsheets; they live in unglamorous supply chains where solving a messy origin problem earns decades of pricing power.
epigraph.author: Research Desk Prologue

web_blocks.html: Manorama Industries Limited (NSE: MANORAMA) is India’s largest producer of exotic tree-borne specialty fats and Cocoa Butter Equivalents (CBE) [14, 19]. It operates a 47,500 MTPA fractionation plant in Birkoni, Chhattisgarh, backed by sourcing subsidiaries across West Africa [5, 16]. The company collects wild sal seeds and mango kernels in India alongside shea nuts in the Sahel [14, 16]. It refines those fats into precision stearin and olein for global chocolate and personal-care giants such as Ferrero, Mondelez, Hershey, and Barry Callebaut [19].

Our price-blind audit (Chapters 1–6) graded the business COMPOUNDER_PASS with kpi_health = PASS_WITH_WATCH. In FY26, revenue rose 57% YoY to ₹1,367 crore with a 26.4% operating margin and 34.9% ROCE [1]. Operating cash flow reached ₹250 crore (92% of EBITDA), yielding ₹196 crore in free cash flow [1]. Momentum continued in Q2 FY27 as sales grew 41.9% YoY to ₹458.9 crore (~85% volume-led) and PAT rose 51.8% to ₹80.8 crore [28, 29]. Key watch items remain the 369-day inventory cycle, H1 debt spikes (₹518 crore in Sep 2026), single-site Birkoni concentration, and Sahel logistics [1, 5, 6, 16].

web_blocks.takeaway: MANORAMA earns WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT for new capital (waiting for ₹1,870–₹1,960 stabilization after 6 distribution days) and KEEP_COMPOUNDING for the 85 held shares, backed by 34.9% ROCE, ₹500 Cr QIP liquidity, and an intact Stage 2 weekly floor.

book_paragraphs: Imagine standing at the edge of a sal forest in Chhattisgarh during the brief six-week summer harvest, watching thousands of tribal collectors gather fallen seeds that most industrial buyers consider too scattered and messy to touch. Now follow those seeds into a 47,500-tonne fractionation plant in Birkoni, where they are transformed into ultra-pure cocoa butter equivalents that melt at exact human body temperature inside a European chocolate bar. That is Manorama Industries—and that messy, hard-to-copy origin network is the core reason we are sitting down to underwrite it from scratch.

To keep ourselves honest, we ran a strict two-pass audit. In Chapters 1 through 6, we locked the stock ticker and valuation multiples out of the room and judged the business strictly on its factories, customer approvals, tribal and West African supply chains, CEO walk-the-talk record, and ten-year cash conversion. Manorama earned a COMPOUNDER_PASS with a watch flag on its seasonal working capital: FY26 revenue hit ₹1,367 crore with a 26.4% operating margin, 34.9% ROCE, and ₹196 crore of free cash flow, while Q2 FY27 kept the momentum rolling with ₹458.9 crore in sales (+41.9% YoY, 85% volume-driven) and ₹80.8 crore in net profit.

Only after locking that business reality did we open the market tape as of Friday, November 13, 2026. At ₹1,984.10 (₹12,528 crore market cap, 44.1x Screener P/E), the stock is not cheap on trailing optics, but a Reverse DCF shows the market is pricing in roughly 20.5% ten-year revenue compounding at 22.5% normalized margins—hurdles Manorama is currently clearing with room to spare. Even better, Friday's -5.52% high-volume pullback dropped the stock right back into its Stage 2 moving-average shelf, only 4.54% above its 10-week EMA.

Our independent verdict is clear and disciplined. For new capital, we tighten from chasing Friday’s -5.52% heavy-volume drop to WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT—waiting for price to stabilize inside the ₹1,870–₹1,960 moving-average shelf and confirm an intraday turn after six distribution days in 25 sessions. Against our ₹1,664 structural stop and ₹2,520 base target, that support zone offers 1.89-to-1 asymmetry. For your existing 85 shares in Zerodha (₹1,68,648.50 market value, +7.01% gain, 3.92% portfolio weight), the action remains KEEP_COMPOUNDING with zero shares sold.

Let us also be crystal clear about how we treat the capital sitting on the sidelines. In a portfolio worth ₹42,97,450.80 with ₹5,74,581.75 in liquid cash, every incremental rupee has to compete across three doors: active shortlist setups, outside researched peers, and cash. Because the broader Indian market sits in an Uptrend with narrow breadth and three distribution days, we do not spray cash indiscriminately. For the next marginal ₹1,00,000 cash unit, we allocate 40% to shortlist peer ZYDUSLIFE (₹1,189.90, Stage 2 CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION toward ₹1,352.43 with a ₹1,091.67 stop), 0% to outside peer FINEORG (₹5,299.50, 33.7x P/E, 21.5% ROCE), and keep 60% in cash—preserving dry powder to add to Manorama if it tests ₹1,870–₹1,960.
